# Test fixtures

Everything here is generated by the float64 oracle in `tools/` and checked in. Never edit a
file by hand; regenerate and review the diff.

| fixture | generator | check |
|---|---|---|
| `qwen35-tiny/` | `python3 tools/make_tiny.py` | `python3 tools/make_tiny.py --check` |
| `ops/*.json` | `python3 tools/make_ops.py` | `python3 tools/make_ops.py --check` |

`--check` regenerates in memory and fails unless every file is byte-identical and no extra file is
present. Both generators are deterministic (seeded `random.Random`, no clocks, no environment).

## `qwen35-tiny/`

A complete Qwen3.5-shaped checkpoint small enough for unit tests. Seed 8 (constant `SEED` in
`tools/make_tiny.py`, found with `--find-seed`). About 1.5 MB.

| file | content |
|---|---|
| `config.json` | real schema: nested `text_config` (same keys, same order as the real 4B config), `model_type` `qwen3_5`, `layer_types`, `full_attention_interval` 4, `rope_parameters` (theta 1e7, partial_rotary_factor 0.25, mrope_section [2,1,1]); other top-level keys (`vision_config`, token ids) as in the real file |
| `model.safetensors-0000{1,2}-of-00002.safetensors` + `model.safetensors.index.json` | two shards, real tensor names with prefix `model.language_model.`. Shard 1: embedding and layers 0-3. Shard 2: layers 4-7, final norm, and tensors the engine MUST ignore: `model.visual.*` (5 tensors) and `mtp.*` (3 tensors) |
| `model.q8.safetensors` | `tools/quant_ref.py` output for the dir above (format in the `quant_ref.py` docstring) |
| `golden_bf16.json`, `golden_q8.json` | oracle results, schema below |

Dimensions: 8 layers (indices 3 and 7 are full attention, the rest linear), hidden 64,
intermediate 128, vocab 384, 4 heads x 32 with 2 KV heads, rotary dim 8 (partial 0.25), linear
attention 2 key heads x 16 and 4 value heads x 16, conv kernel 4, eps 1e-6, tied embeddings.

dtypes: every tensor is BF16 (values exactly representable) EXCEPT
`...linear_attn.A_log`, which is F32, so both the BF16 and the F32 copy path are exercised. The
real checkpoint's dtype for `A_log` is not known to the oracle author; the engine should accept BF16
and F32 for `A_log`, `dt_bias` and the norms. Tensors: `conv1d.weight` is `[conv_dim, 1, 4]`.

Golden schema (compact JSON, one trailing newline):

```
{"tokens": [24 ints], "logits": [[384 floats] per token],
 "greedy": {"prompt": [first 8 of tokens], "out": [16 ints]}}
```

* `logits[t]` is the output at position t after feeding `tokens[0..t]` from a zero state.
  Floats are float64 oracle values printed with 9 significant digits (round-trips f32).
* `greedy.out` are the next 16 ids by argmax (lowest id wins ties), feeding each back.
* `golden_bf16.json`: weights from the shards. `golden_q8.json`: the oracle on the weights
  dequantised from `model.q8.safetensors` ((double)q * (double)scale), so both are exact targets.
* Margins, asserted by the generator for BOTH goldens: top-1 minus top-2 logit above 0.05 (plan asks
  for 1e-2) at all 24 positions and all 16 greedy steps (actual minima: bf16 0.100, q8 0.083); max
  |logit| about 19; gate tolerance 2e-4 * max|row| is about 4e-3; q8 and bf16 logits differ by up to 5.2.
* `lm-run --tokens <tokens> --logits-out F` must produce 24 rows; `--tokens <prompt> --greedy 16`
  must print `greedy.out`. `tools/check_golden.py` does exactly this.

## `ops/*.json`

Compact JSON, one file per op. All activations are f32-exact, all weights bf16-exact; expected
outputs are float64 (a C test with f32 math should compare with about
`1e-5 * max(1, max|y|)`; the q8 file is exact). Every file has `"op"` and `"formula"` or `"note"`.

* `rmsnorm.json`: `eps`, `cases` of `{x[n], w[n], y[n]}`. `y = x * rsqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) * (1+w)`.
  n in 1, 7, 16, 33, 64, 256; one all-zero x; one tiny x (1e-4 scale).
* `rmsnorm_gated.json`: `eps`, `cases` of `{x, z, w, y}`; `y = x * rsqrt(mean(x^2)+eps) * w * silu(z)`.
  `w` is PLAIN (no `1+`).
* `l2norm.json`: `eps` 1e-6, `cases` of `{x, y}`, `y = x * rsqrt(sum(x^2)+eps)`; includes zero and tiny x.
* `rope.json`: `groups` of `{head_dim, rot_dim, theta, cases:[{pos, x[head_dim], y[head_dim]}]}`.
  Rotate-half on the first `rot_dim` entries, the rest unchanged. Groups: 32/8/1e7 (positions up to
  4093), 256/64/1e7 (real shape, positions up to 100000), 16/16/100, 24/6/10000.
* `conv1d_silu.json`: `cases` of `{channels, kernel, weight[channels][kernel], x[T][channels],
  y[T][channels], split, state_at_split[kernel-1][channels]}`. Causal depthwise conv then SiLU, zero
  initial state; `weight[c][kernel-1]` multiplies the current input. `state_at_split` holds the
  `kernel-1` inputs before position `split` (oldest first): starting a fresh run at `x[split:]` with
  that state must give `y[split:]`.
* `gated_delta_rule.json`: `cases` of `{num_k_heads, num_v_heads, dk, dv, steps:[{q[nk*dk], k[nk*dk],
  v[nv*dv], g[nv], beta[nv], o[nv*dv]}], final_state[nv][dk][dv]}`. `q`, `k` are the RAW post-conv
  values: the op applies `l2norm(eps 1e-6)` per key head and scales `q` by `1/sqrt(dk)`. `g` is the
  already computed log-decay (<= 0), `beta` the already computed sigmoid. Value head `i` uses key head
  `i / (nv/nk)` (consecutive). State `S[dk][dv]` starts at zero. Cases: 2x4 heads 16/16 (10 steps),
  1x3 heads 8/12 (6 steps), 2x2 heads (5 steps).
* `full_attention_layer.json`: `{hidden 32, heads 4, kv_heads 2, head_dim 16, rot_dim 8, theta 100, eps,
  weights, x[8][32], y[8][32]}`. Mixer only (no residual, no input norm; `x` is already normed).
  `weights` keys are `q_proj.weight` `[heads*head_dim*2][hidden]` (per head: query rows then gate rows),
  `k_proj.weight`, `v_proj.weight` `[kv_heads*head_dim][hidden]`, `o_proj.weight` `[hidden][heads*head_dim]`,
  `q_norm.weight`, `k_norm.weight` `[head_dim]`. Includes per-head q/gate split, q_norm/k_norm,
  partial RoPE at position t for `x[t]`, causal GQA softmax attention, sigmoid output gate.
* `linear_attention_layer.json`: `{hidden 32, num_k_heads 2, num_v_heads 4, key_head_dim 8,
  value_head_dim 8, conv_kernel 4, eps, weights, x[8][32], y[8][32]}`. Mixer only. `weights`:
  `in_proj_qkv.weight`, `in_proj_z.weight`, `in_proj_b.weight`, `in_proj_a.weight`, `conv1d.weight`
  (`[conv_dim][kernel]`, the `[C,1,K]` tensor squeezed), `dt_bias`, `A_log`, `norm.weight` (plain,
  `[value_head_dim]`), `out_proj.weight`. Zero conv and recurrent state before `x[0]`.
* `mlp.json`: `{hidden 32, intermediate 48, weights{gate_proj.weight, up_proj.weight,
  down_proj.weight}, x[4][32], y[4][32]}`, `y = down(silu(gate(x)) * up(x))`.
* `q8_quantize.json`: `{group 32, groups:[{name, x[32], x_bf16_bits[32], scale, scale_f32_bits, q[32]}],
  matrix:{rows 3, cols 96, x[288], q[288], scale[9], scale_f32_bits[9]}}`. Groups: `ties_at_half_scale_1`
  (scale exactly 1.0, ties at .5 round to even), `zero_group`, `negative_zero_group`,
  `negative_zero_with_values`, `max_negative_at_clamp`, `max_positive_at_clamp`, `scale_not_exact`,
  `tiny_values`, `bf16_subnormal_scale` (scale is an f32 subnormal: no flush-to-zero),
  `huge_values`, `random_0..5`. `matrix` row-major `[rows][cols]`, scales `[rows][cols/32]`, the third
  group of row 0 is all zero (scale 0).

Floating point in these files is Python `repr`, which round-trips doubles exactly.
